title: Lower quasi-coherent tensor tests for an upper bounded algebraic-space complex
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $S$ with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Derived tensor and pullback use K-flat resolutions with flat terms; derived direct image uses K-injective resolutions. Let $Y$ be quasi-separated, meaning that its diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $K\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ have quasi-coherent cohomology, let $c\in\mathbf Z$, and assume $H^i(K)=0$ for $i>c$. For any integer $a\le c$, the following are equivalent: (1) $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,c]$, meaning $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Y}G[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $G$ and every $i\notin[a,c]$; (2) for every quasi-coherent module sheaf $F$, one has $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_Y}F[0])=0$ for every $i<a$.

source.place: Tag 08IL (lemma-tor-qc-qs), together with the elementary upper derived-tensor bound used in Tag 08IS (lemma-perfect-direct-image), proof sentence "Bounded from above is clear as Rf_*(E) is bounded from above".

proof.text: First establish the upper bound for every module sheaf $G$, independently of condition (2). Represent $K$ by a complex $C^\bullet$ and replace it by the good truncation $C'=\tau_{\le c}C$: its terms are $C^i$ for $i<c$, $\ker(d^c)$ in degree $c$, and zero for $i>c$. Its inclusion into $C$ induces the same cohomology through degree $c$ and both cohomologies vanish above $c$, hence it represents $K$. The site flat-resolution theorem supplies a functorial flat cover of every module. Flat modules contain zero and are closed under isomorphisms, finite sums and direct summands: tensoring a finite sum is the sum of the tensor functors, and a summand of an exact functor remains exact. Apply the bounded-above class-resolution theorem to the flat class and $C'$, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C'$ with flat terms and $P^i=0$ for $i>c$. The bounded-above flat K-flatness theorem makes $P$ K-flat. Therefore $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}G[0]$ is represented by $P\otimes G$, whose degree $i$ term is $P^i\otimes G$ and is zero for $i>c$. Thus its cohomology vanishes for every $i>c$.

source.place: Tag 08IS (lemma-perfect-direct-image), upper-bound sentence; bound-preserving flat replacement uses derived.tex Tag 05T7 (lemma-subcategory-left-resolution), and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat).

proof.text: Condition (1) immediately implies condition (2): every quasi-coherent module sheaf is a module sheaf, and $i<a$ implies $i\notin[a,c]$. Conversely assume (2). Together with step 1 it says that $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}F[0]$ has cohomology only in $[a,c]$ for every quasi-coherent $F$.

source.place: Tag 08IL, (1) implies (2), and initialization of its converse.

proof.text: Let $j:U\to Y$ be any affine etale scheme chart and let $G$ be a quasi-coherent module on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. The affine-chart geometry lemma gives quasi-compactness and separatedness of $j$ from the quasi-separatedness of $Y$. The quasi-coherent pushforward theorem then gives that $j_*G$ is quasi-coherent. Applying step 2 to this particular test yields $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}j_*G[0])=0$ for $i\notin[a,c]$.

source.place: Tag 08IL, first paragraph of converse: apply quasi-coherent pushforward, spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward).

proof.text: Etale pullback is exact restriction to the slice site, so it commutes with kernels and cokernels and hence with cohomology of any complex. The derived tensor-pullback comparison identifies the restriction of the tensor object in step 3 with $j^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*j_*G[0]$. Its cohomology therefore vanishes outside $[a,c]$. The split-counit lemma supplies $s:G\to j^*j_*G$ and $r:j^*j_*G\to G$ with $rs=1$. Apply the functor $H^i(j^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}(-)[0])$: it preserves this equality of composites. Its value on $G$ is consequently a retract of zero, so its identity is zero and it vanishes. We have proved the full interval test for every quasi-coherent $G$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Also $j^*K$ has quasi-coherent cohomology by the derived chart calculus.

source.place: Tag 08IL, first paragraph of converse: flat pullback and direct-summand reduction; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 0HAP (lemma-etale-pull-push-split).

proof.text: Use the Zariski-etale equivalence on the scheme $U$ to write $j^*K\simeq\epsilon_U^*K_0$ with $K_0\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})$. For every quasi-coherent Zariski module $F_0$, exactness of $\epsilon_U^*$ and its $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ equivalence show that $\epsilon_U^*F_0$ is quasi-coherent. The derived tensor-pullback comparison and exactness identify the pullback of $H^i(K_0\otimes^{\mathbf L}F_0[0])$ with $H^i(j^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\epsilon_U^*F_0[0])$. The latter vanishes outside $[a,c]$ by step 4. Faithfulness of $\epsilon_U^*$ on all module sheaves implies the former Zariski cohomology sheaf is zero: a faithful functor sending its identity to zero forces that identity to be zero.

The affine scheme $U$ is quasi-separated, and $a\le c$ by hypothesis. Apply the scheme quasi-coherent Tor test to $K_0$ and the tests of step 5. It gives Tor amplitude $[a,c]$ for $K_0$ against every Zariski module. The Zariski-etale Tor-amplitude comparison then gives Tor amplitude $[a,c]$ for $\epsilon_U^*K_0\simeq j^*K$ against every etale module on $U$.

source.place: Tag 08IL, last sentence, using perfect.tex Tag 08EA (lemma-tor-qc-qs); return to the etale site by Tag 08HF (lemma-descend-tor-amplitude).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary module sheaf $G$ on $Y$ and $i\notin[a,c]$. For each affine etale chart $j:U\to Y$, exact restriction and the derived tensor comparison identify $j^*H^i(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}G[0])$ with $H^i(j^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}j^*G[0])$, which is zero by step 6. Every etale scheme over $Y$ has an affine open covering; its members are affine etale charts of $Y$. A section of the cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on these members, so is zero by the uniqueness clause of the sheaf axiom. Thus the cohomology sheaf itself is zero. This holds for all $G$ and $i\notin[a,c]$, which is condition (1).

source.place: Tag 08IL, first paragraph: it suffices to prove the amplitude on every affine etale chart; explicit sheaf gluing.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08IL (lemma-tor-qc-qs), both paragraphs, with the upper bound made explicit by bounded-above flat replacement as used in Tag 08IS.
